description: Compulsory education is a legal duty on parents or guardians to have children schooled. Prussian decrees of 1717 and the General School Regulation of 1763 required attendance, though enforcement long lagged behind the law. Massachusetts passed an attendance law in 1852. uncertainty: Earlier school ordinances (for example in Protestant German territories and Scotland in the seventeenth century) also demanded schooling, so which law counts as the first is debated; actual attendance rose slowly and unevenly after each law.
